skill.description: UI/UX reference skill for designing and reviewing interfaces across web and mobile stacks. It provides searchable guidance for styles, color palettes, typography, charts, landing page structure, UX patterns, and frontend best practices.
skill.summary: Search a bundled UI/UX knowledge base for practical design, accessibility, and frontend implementation guidance.
skill.author: DCjanus

security_audit.summary: All 379 static findings were adjudicated as false positives. The alerts are caused by CSV reference rows, documentation URLs, Markdown backticks, frontend examples, and UI guidance text. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, malicious network access, hidden binaries, or unsafe command execution.

remediation.issue: Static analysis noise from example code and documentation URLs in reference CSV files.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples clearly labeled as reference data and avoid adding executable snippets outside the local search helper.

remediation.issue: Markdown instructions ask agents to run a local Python search helper.
remediation.suggestion: Document that the helper only reads bundled CSV files and uses fixed domain and stack choices.

remediation.issue: Next.js guidance mentions environment variables and secret file names.
remediation.suggestion: Continue using placeholder examples only, and never include real credentials or private environment values.

content.user_title: Design Better UI with UX Reference Data
content.value_statement: Interface work often needs fast choices about style, layout, color, typography, and accessibility. This skill searches a curated UI/UX reference database and turns results into practical design guidance.
actual_capabilities: Searches bundled CSV data for UI styles, product patterns, colors, typography, charts, and landing page structures.
Provides implementation guidance for React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, SwiftUI, React Native, Flutter, and Tailwind.
Suggests accessibility, layout, animation, contrast, spacing, hover, focus, and responsive design improvements.
Maps product types such as SaaS, e-commerce, dashboards, portfolios, and mobile apps to suitable design directions.
Uses local Python search helpers to retrieve relevant guidance from bundled reference files.
limitations: It does not replace product research, brand approval, or a human design review.
It cannot verify visual output unless the host agent renders and checks the interface.
Its recommendations are limited to the bundled reference database unless the agent uses other sources.
Complex products may require multiple searches across product, style, UX, and stack domains.

use_cases.title: Plan a Product Interface
use_cases.description: Choose a style direction, palette, typography, layout structure, and UX checks for a new product screen.

use_cases.title: Improve Frontend Polish
use_cases.description: Review components for spacing, contrast, hover states, focus states, responsive behavior, and stack-specific best practices.

use_cases.title: Shape a Landing Page
use_cases.description: Find a landing page structure, conversion pattern, chart choice, and visual language for a launch or campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Style Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ui-ux-pro-max to suggest a style, palette, typography, and layout for a healthcare SaaS dashboard. Keep the recommendations practical.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing UI
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for critique and fixes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this interface with ui-ux-pro-max. Focus on hierarchy, spacing, contrast, hover states, focus states, accessibility, and responsive behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design for a Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ui-ux-pro-max to design a Next.js landing page for a fintech product. Include stack-specific guidance, UX risks, and a concise implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Design System Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ui-ux-pro-max across product, style, color, typography, UX, chart, and stack domains to create a design system plan for a multi-page analytics product.

output_examples.input: Design a landing page for a premium skincare service.
output: Recommended direction: elegant minimal layout with soft contrast and refined photography.
Use a calm beauty palette, high-contrast body text, serif headings, and clear appointment CTAs.
Structure the page around hero, services, proof, pricing, testimonials, and booking sections.
Check mobile spacing, tap targets, focus states, reduced motion, and image alt text before delivery.

output_examples.input: Review a React dashboard for accessibility and polish.
output: Prioritize semantic navigation, visible focus states, stable card hover effects, and accessible table labels.
Use chart types that match the data relationship and avoid color-only status indicators.
Test at small, tablet, laptop, and wide desktop widths before final handoff.

output_examples.input: Choose typography and colors for a modern SaaS app.
output: Use a neutral interface palette with one clear action color and sufficient text contrast.
Pair a clean sans heading family with a readable body family to support dense product screens.
Document button, form, table, sidebar, and chart usage so later screens remain consistent.

best_practices: Search product, style, color, typography, UX, and stack data before making final UI choices.
Clarify the audience, brand tone, platform, and technical stack when they are unclear.
Render and test responsive states, focus states, contrast, and motion after applying recommendations.
anti_patterns: Using one style keyword as the complete design brief.
Skipping accessibility, contrast, keyboard, and reduced-motion checks.
Applying examples from one stack to another without adapting framework conventions.

faq.question: What can this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan, build, review, and improve UI/UX decisions using bundled reference data.

faq.question: Does it generate final UI code?
faq.answer: It provides guidance that an AI coding agent can use to create or improve interface code.

faq.question: Which stacks are covered?
faq.answer: It covers React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, SwiftUI, React Native, Flutter, and HTML with Tailwind.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: The core search uses local CSV files. Some returned references include documentation or font URLs.

faq.question: Can it check accessibility?
faq.answer: It can suggest accessibility checks for contrast, semantics, focus, labels, keyboard use, and reduced motion.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: Designers, frontend engineers, founders, and product teams can use it for faster UI decisions.
